name: September
summary: September brings quieter school-year weekdays at some parks and Halloween events opening from September 11 onward. Check each park's operating calendar before choosing a visit date.

verdict.short: September can offer quieter ride days, while Halloween events start on different dates and often bring larger evening crowds.
bestFor: Weekday ride days at their calmest
worstFor: Weekend crowd levels once haunts start
Reduced weekday hours at some parks

crowds.shape: School-year weekdays can be calmer, while Halloween programs open from September 11 onward and lift selected evenings and weekends.
peakWindows: Select Halloween opening nights and weekends
quietWindows: The first three weeks' weekdays — the year's calmest full-operation days

cost.note: Ticket prices move by date at every park on this site; the level describes the month's overall shape rather than any single day.

planningNotes.heading: The month in one decision
body: The September weekday is this site's single best product: summer operation, school-year crowds, and weather that has stopped trying to kill you at the Texas parks.

planningNotes.heading: The detail that matters
body: Halloween events begin on different dates from September 11 onward. A daytime family program and a nighttime haunt can have different admission and activity rules on the same park date.

freshness.sourceNote: Crowd and cost shapes describe multi-year patterns across the ten parks rather than a forecast for any single year. Weather figures are climate normals for each region and do not decay; the Texas figures blend the DFW and San Antonio areas, and the Southern California figures blend the coastal and inland valleys.
